items.stem: What does the term 'goods' refer to in the passage?
According to the passage, what is the main reason individuals must make choices?
If a society produces more corn than people want, what should happen?
What is the central problem of an economy according to the passage?
What does the passage mean when it says that resources have competing usages?
If an economy decides to produce more education services, what is likely to happen?
An economy produces 3 units of corn and 4 units of cotton. If it wants to increase cotton production by 2 units, what will happen?
Why does the passage say that the production possibility frontier is a curve?
What is the main idea of the passage?
What is the purpose of a market according to the passage?
What does the production possibility frontier illustrate?
In which type of economy does the government make all major decisions?
Which of the following best describes a mixed economy?
What is the role of prices in a market economy?
Why is opportunity cost important in economics?
Which of the following is an example of a question studied in macroeconomics?
What are the two broad branches of economics studied in the passage?
Which of the following is a branch of economics that studies the behavior of individual economic agents?
If a student is studying the market for a single commodity, which branch of economics is he most likely studying?
What is the main focus of macroeconomics?
If a country is experiencing rising prices and high unemployment, which branch of economics would study this phenomenon?
Which of the following is an example of an aggregate measure studied in macroeconomics?
What is the main way that a centrally planned economy makes decisions about production, exchange, and consumption?
A student is asked to explain the difference between microeconomics and macroeconomics. Which of the following best captures the core distinction between the two?
Which of the following best describes the role of price in a market economy?
If a government decides to provide more education and health services in an economy, which type of economic system is most likely to do this?
What is the key difference between a market economy and a centrally planned economy?
In a market economy, what is the likely effect of an increase in the demand for a product?
Why might an economy be described as a mixed economy?
What is the central problem of an economy according to the passage?
What does the passage say about the production possibility frontier?
According to the passage, what is the opportunity cost of producing more of one good?
Which of the following best defines a 'resource' in economics?
A family farm produces corn and uses part of it for consumption. It exchanges the rest for clothing and housing. Which of the following best describes the economic problem faced by the family farm?
If a family farm produces corn and wants to obtain clothing, what must it do?
If a country is studying how its overall employment level changes over time, which branch of economics is it most likely focusing on?
What is the main challenge in the allocation of resources in an economy?
